## Correctness

### no-circular

_Category: correctness, `error` by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports dependencies that are part of a circular chain of imports and
shows the shortest cycle through each of them.

#### Why is this bad?

Cycles make modules impossible to load, test or reason about in
isolation, and can cause `undefined` values at runtime.

#### Options

`includeTypeOnly`: also count type-only imports, which are erased at runtime. Off by
default, so a cycle that exists only through `import type` is not reported.

`ignore`: globs of modules removed from the graph before cycles are searched, for example
a barrel file everything legitimately goes through. Use `overrides` to scope the rule to
some files instead.

`maxCyclesPerComponent`: a large tangle of modules has one cycle per dependency, and
finding each costs a search of the whole tangle. Only this many dependencies per strongly
connected component (the first ones in graph order, 100 by default) are searched; one
extra violation on the component's first module says how many were left out. `0` searches
them all.

### no-cross-package-relative

_Category: correctness, `error` by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports relative imports (`../other-package/src/x`) that reach into another workspace package.

#### Why is this bad?

Packages should depend on each other through their package name so the dependency is
declared in `package.json` and the package boundary is respected.

### no-dev-deps-in-prod

_Category: correctness, `error` by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports production modules importing packages that are only in `devDependencies`.

#### Why is this bad?

Dev dependencies are not installed in production, so the import fails there.
Type-only imports are fine and are ignored.

#### Options

`prod` and `test` are path patterns that say which modules are production and which are tests.

### no-test-imports

_Category: correctness, `error` by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports non-test modules importing test files (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`) or test
directories (`test`, `tests`, `__tests__`, `__mocks__`).

#### Why is this bad?

Test code and its dependencies end up in the production bundle, or crash there.

### no-undeclared-deps

_Category: correctness, `error` by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports imports of installed npm packages that no `package.json` section declares.

#### Why is this bad?

The import only works because of hoisting or a transitive install, and
breaks when the dependency tree changes.

### no-unresolvable

_Category: correctness, `error` by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports imports that could not be resolved to a file or package.

#### Options

`ignore`: globs matched against the import specifier and the importing module's path,
for virtual modules and generated code.

## Suspicious

### no-deprecated

_Category: suspicious, `warn` by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports imports of Node.js built-in modules that Node has deprecated, such as `sys` or
`punycode`, and of npm packages whose `package.json` marks them as deprecated.

### no-duplicate-deps

_Category: suspicious, `warn` by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports packages declared in more than one `package.json` section, for example both
`dependencies` and `devDependencies`. Type-only imports are ignored.

### no-orphans

_Category: suspicious, `warn` by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports modules that no other module imports and that import nothing.

#### Why is this bad?

An orphan is usually dead code left behind by a refactor.

#### Options

`ignore`: globs for modules that are legitimately unconnected. They extend the built-in
list: dotfiles (`**/.*`), declaration files (`**/*.d.ts`), `**/tsconfig*.json` and tool
configuration (`**/*.config.*`).

## Restriction

### internal-modules

_Category: restriction, off by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Go-style `internal` directories: code under `a/b/internal/` may only be imported from code under `a/b/`.

### layers

_Category: restriction, off by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Enforces a layered architecture: each layer may import only the layers it lists in `allow`.

#### Example

```json
{ "layers": { "ui": "src/ui/**", "domain": "src/domain/**" },
  "allow":  { "ui": ["domain"], "domain": [] } }
```

### no-optional-deps

_Category: restriction, off by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports use of optional dependencies, which may not be installed.

### no-peer-deps

_Category: restriction, off by default. Since 0.1.0._

#### What it does

Reports use of peer dependencies, which the consuming project must provide.
